checklist.evidence: Title is legible in every frame, centred, pale mint on near-black.

checklist.item: visible glitch artefacts (RGB split, block displacement, scanlines or noise)
checklist.evidence: Frames at 0.75s, 1.25s, 4.25s and 5.75s show RGB fringing and sliced or displaced blocks across the letters.

The effect only reaches the text. The background stays flat black with barely visible noise, with no scanlines, roll bars, static bursts or screen distortion, so it reads as a glitchy title and not a broken TV.

problems: The broken-TV look is weak. The background is almost pure black with no visible scanlines, static, tracking bars or screen distortion.
The subtitle 'ERR 0x0000F4 // SIGNAL LOST' is tiny, dim and low-contrast, and is often unreadable once glitched.
The title takes up only about 60% of the frame width, and the large empty black space makes the composition feel small and plain.
The glitch is subtle and uniform between bursts. Frames such as 1.75s and 2.75s show a clean title with no impact, so the glitch lacks drama.
Colour is limited to mint and a muted red, so the palette is flat and generic.
judge.verdict: The title is legible and has some RGB-split and slice glitching. It looks like a glitchy text effect more than a broken TV, and the subtitle is too small and dim. It is acceptable but generic, and the user would probably ask for a stronger TV-failure look.
